profile.name: Singo Ulung
profile.tagline: A traditional lion dance from the Bondowoso regency of East Java, Indonesia.
profile.insight: Created by the first head of Blimbing village, Mbah Singo Wulu, this lion dance uses costumes crafted from decomposed raffia string to honor the village's founding spirit.
profile.profile: Singo Ulung is a traditional dance from Bondowoso, East Java, performed by two dancers inside a lion-shaped costume. It serves as a central ritual for the annual Bersih Desa purification ceremony in Blimbing village. The performance, which also features characters like Panji and warok dancers, is a key cultural marker of the region's history.
profile.profile_long:
Singo Ulung originates from the Bondowoso regency in East Java, where it is performed as a traditional art form. The dance was created by a man named Singo Wulu, who arrived in Blimbing village from Ponorogo and eventually became the village's first head. He worked alongside his wife, Nyi Moena, and a man named Ki Jasiman to improve the lives of the local community, leading to the creation of this public performance.

The dance is performed by two people operating a lion-like costume, known as a barongan. The costume is constructed from raffia string that has been decomposed to resemble fur, typically appearing in white, black and white, or yellow and white. Other performers in the ensemble include characters dressed in the style of Tari Topeng, female dancers in traditional kebaya and sampur, and warok dancers dressed in black with red-white shirts, carrying a whip known as a cemethi.

Singo Ulung is a vital component of the annual Bersih Desa ritual in Blimbing, held during the month of Sya'ban or Ruwah to honor the village's founding spirit and the goddess of rice, Sri. The performance is also featured during the anniversary of the Bondowoso regency on August 16. Today, the dance is preserved by local art galleries and performed at festivals and guest-welcoming events to introduce the public to Bondowoso's cultural heritage.

sections.origins_and_history: The dance was created by Singo Wulu, a man from Ponorogo who settled in Blimbing village, Klabang district, and served as its first village head.
sections.how_it_is_danced: The dance is performed by two people inside a lion costume, accompanied by other characters including Panji, Jasiman, and warok dancers. Specific footwork and movement technique not described in sources.
sections.music_and_instruments: The dance is accompanied by particular music designed to impress the audience. Specific instruments and musical structure not described in sources.
sections.costume_and_setting: The lion costume is made of raffia string. Warok dancers wear black with red-white shirts and carry a cemethi, while female dancers wear kebaya and sampur.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: The dance is performed annually at the Bersih Desa ritual in Blimbing village and at the Bondowoso anniversary on August 16.
sections.notable_figures: Singo Wulu (the creator and first head of Blimbing village), Nyi Moena, and Ki Jasiman.

profile.sacred_note: The dance is a required element of the Bersih Desa ritual ceremony in Blimbing village and is considered a main means that cannot be replaced.

claims.text: Singo Ulung is a traditional dance from the Bondowoso regency of East Java.
claims.quote: Singo Ulung (Javanese: ꦱꦶꦔꦲꦸꦭꦸꦁ, romanized: Singa Ulung, Javanese pronunciation: [siːŋɔ ʊlʊŋ]) is one of the original traditional dances from Bondowoso regency, East Java, Indonesia.

claims.text: The dance was created by Singo Wulu, who became the first head of Blimbing village.
claims.quote: That's why he was chosen to become the first head of Blimbing village. One day, he had an idea to create a public traditional dance called Singo Ulung

claims.text: The lion costume is made of raffia string.
claims.quote: The material of the costume is raffia string, decomposed until it looks like fur.

claims.text: The dance is performed during the annual Bersih Desa ritual in Blimbing village.
claims.quote: This art, Pojian art, and Ojung art are always shown at the traditional ceremony of Bersih Desa Blimbing held every year in the month of Syaban / Ruwah

claims.text: Singo Ulung is also performed during the anniversary of Bondowoso on August 16.
claims.quote: On the other hand, this art performance can be enjoyed in the annual moment of Hari Jadi Bondowoso, precisely on 16 August.

claims.text: The dance is considered a necessary part of the village ritual ceremony.
claims.quote: It is necessary to perform Singo Ulung in the ritual village ceremony because it is considered a main means and cannot be replaced by others.
